# Final Touches — Murim Login

## Goal

Prepare one mastered chapter for readers. This pass adds footnotes, repairs formatting, and fixes duplicate or missing sentences. It is not a fluency rewrite.

Keep the mastered prose. Change a sentence only to attach a footnote, repair System / thought / speech / chat formatting, restore a source sentence the English dropped, or remove an English sentence the Korean does not support.

## Duplicates and omissions

Compare the English with the Korean source.

- Restore source facts, events, dialogue, and sentences the English dropped, in the same place in the scene.
- Remove English sentences that have no support in the Korean.
- Keep a bold label that names a quoted document, manual, warning, or sign, such as `> **Warning**`. Keep it when this chapter recalls or reprints a notice that was labeled earlier, even if the Korean reprint shows only the body.
- Keep repetition the Korean itself repeats: comedy, panic, emphasis, echoed dialogue, and short beats such as `……`.
- Do not treat a short refrain or a deliberate echo as a duplicate.

## Footnotes

Use Markdown footnotes (`[^1]`, `[^2]`, …). Number them in order of first appearance, starting at 1 for this chapter. Put every definition in one block at the end of the file.

Within this chapter, write one definition for a term, unit, amount, or reference. Every later occurrence of that same thing reuses the same marker. `goshiwon` five times is one note, and so is `hyung`. A different amount or a different term gets its own note. Another chapter may carry its own note for the same term.

Write notes in factual English. No spoilers and no jokes added by the note. Romanize words. A note may include the original character when it is explaining that character. Keep Hangul jamo already used as chat reactions, such as ㅋㅋ and ㄷㄷ.

Add a note only when an English reader would otherwise miss the meaning or the conversion. Skip it when the sentence already says what the reference means. A translated proverb whose warning is plain, a joke the next line completes, a place name used as a place, and a fictional law the dialogue already describes do not get notes.

Skip a conversion footnote when the prose already states both metric and imperial for that quantity.

### Won

Footnote Korean won, including round figures and vague amounts (“hundreds of millions of won”), when the prose does not already give the conversion. Use only the project rates in the packet. Show dollars, then euros, as approximate figures. Round large amounts to about two significant figures and say “about.” For a vague amount, give the approximate range those words cover. One note per distinct amount; reuse it for every later mention of that same amount.

Do not convert traditional money (nyang, taels, cash) or Chinese yuan with the won rate. Explain those with a cultural or historical note only when the English does not already carry the meaning.

### Units

Footnote a Korean or Chinese traditional unit, or a metric quantity, once in the chapter, with both metric and imperial, using this table:

| Unit | Use | Metric | Imperial |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pyeong (평) | area | 3.31 m² | 35.6 ft² |
| geun (근) | Korean weight | 600 g | 1.32 lb |
| ja / cheok (자) | length | 30.3 cm | 11.9 in |
| chi (치) | length | 3.03 cm | 1.19 in |
| don (돈) | weight | 3.75 g | 0.132 oz |
| gwan (관) | weight | 3.75 kg | 8.27 lb |
| ri (리), Korea | distance | 393 m | 0.244 mi |
| li (里), China | distance | 500 m | 0.311 mi |
| jin (斤), modern Chinese | weight | 500 g | 1.10 lb |
| liang (两), modern Chinese | weight | 50 g | 1.76 oz |

Choose Korean ri or Chinese li from the setting. Say which one the note uses.

Also footnote metric quantities already in the English (kilometers, meters, centimeters, kilograms, grams, liters, square meters, degrees Celsius) with the imperial equivalent. Use unit words or abbreviations (`ft`, `in`, `mi`, `lb`, `oz`, `gal`). Do not use `"` or `'` as unit marks.

### Cultural references

Footnote a Korean, Chinese, or other Asian word, custom, institution, food, joke, or allusion when the English does not already carry it: `goshiwon`, `hyung`, `doenjang`, `jeonse`. Explain it in one or two sentences. One note per term in the chapter, reused by every later occurrence.

Leave it unnoted when the English is already clear. Do not explain a proverb the translation has already stated, a pun the scene completes, or ordinary vocabulary.

Do not footnote standing series vocabulary. Never add a note whose job is to define any of these, including ordinary variants and compounds:

- Murim
- qi, including demonic qi, innate qi, and qi deviation
- dantian, including the Upper, Middle, and Lower Dantian
- internal energy
- mana

A note about something else may mention these words. Do not attach a marker to them.

## Formatting

Enforce these four patterns. Repair System, speech, thought, and chat formatting when it drifts. Leave every other blockquote heading as it stands.

- **System.** Each real game System panel is one Markdown blockquote headed exactly `> **System**`. Keep the panel’s lines inside that blockquote. Start a new panel only when prose intervenes. Keep every `> **System**` panel from the mastered chapter, including a notice the narrator only hears. Do not turn a panel into italics, a sound effect, or narration. Do not repeat a panel. A notice the mastered chapter already shows more than once stays repeated that many times, and no more. Do not wrap System text in square brackets or label a manual, sign, or ordinary quotation as System. A manual or remembered notice keeps its own label, such as `> **Warning**` or `> **Product User Manual**`. That label is not a System panel, and it is not drift.
- **Speech.** Spoken dialogue uses curly double quotes (`“` `”`). Not straight quotes, not italics.
- **Thoughts.** Direct thoughts are italics with no quotation marks. Keep a mastered thought in italics. Do not turn it into spoken dialogue.
- **Chat and comments.** Public comment threads and private chat logs shown as threads are one blockquote. Each message line begins with `└`, as in `> └ **Name:** message`. Keep a thread title that is not itself a message, such as `> **Peace Guild**`, on its own line above the messages. Do not add a `**Chat**` heading. A status line that is only a name or level, such as `> **Lv. 22 Hyuk Mujin**`, is not a chat message. Leave that line unchanged, including the bold. Ordinary spoken dialogue stays in curly quotes.
- **Headings.** The only Markdown heading is `# Chapter N`. Do not add `##` or `###`. A diary title or similar label stays a bold line, `**Training Day 1**`, even when the mastered copy used a smaller heading.

Leave narration as narration. Scene breaks stay `* * *`, with the same count as the source.

## Output contract

Return only the complete English Markdown chapter. The first nonblank line must be `# Chapter N`. No status line and no model preamble. Do not add Hangul syllables. Chat jamo and a character cited in a note may stay.

## Project conversion rates

These rates are binding. Do not look up or substitute a market rate.

- 1 US dollar = 1400 Korean won
- 1 euro = 1550 Korean won

Convert every won amount with these rates. In each footnote, give dollars first and euros second.

```text
＃319화



“용봉표국의 소국주 주화란이 태을무정검 황보 대협을 뵙습니다.”

주화란은 절도 있게 포권 지례를 취했다.

태을무정검 황보엄, 과연 명불허전이다. 단순히 눈빛을 마주하는 것만으로도 가슴이 조여 오고 숨이 막히는 듯했다.

‘종남제일검(綜南第一劍)…….’

구파일방과 오대세가. 작금의 천하 무림을 지탱하는 열다섯 개의 기둥.

눈앞에 있는 상대는 그들 중 하나인 종남파 제일의 고수다. 그 이름에 실린 막중한 무게감이 그녀를 짓눌렀다.

‘하지만 괜찮아.’

모두가 입을 모아 어렵다고 말하던 표행을 완수했다.

이 자리에 태을무정검이 아니라 풍운검군이 나왔어도 당당할 수 있는 이유였다.

“그래, 의뢰한 물건은 잘 가져왔나?”

“물론입니다.”

주화란은 대답과 함께 품 안에서 천년설삼이 든 목곽을 꺼내 들었다. 목곽 전체를 칭칭 동여맨 새끼줄의 매듭에는 작은 글씨가 쓰여 있었다.



산동(山東) 성수장가(性修長家).



글자를 확인한 황보엄이 고개를 끄덕였다.

“틀림없군. 성수장가의 인(封)이야.”

사람들은 말한다.

사천에 당가(唐家)가 있다면, 산동에는 성수장가가 있다고.

성수장가는 그만큼 의술로 유명한 곳이었다. 무림 세가인 사천당가와 달리 의술에 뿌리를 둔 명망 높은 의가(醫家)이기도 했다.

종남파는 바로 그 성수장가를 통해 천년설삼을 구입, 용봉표국에 운송을 맡겼다.

“성수장가의 현 가주이신 환의(丸醫)께서 직접 천년설삼을 넣으시고 서명하셨습니다.”

“오호, 환의가 직접?”

“예. 뿐만 아니라 저를 포함한 공증인 여럿이 함께 지켜보았지요.”

“나이답지 않게 철두철미하군.”

황보엄의 주름진 손가락이 흰 수염을 쓸어내렸다.

“군자검의 여식이 뛰어난 재녀(才女)라는 말은 노부도 들어서 알고 있지. 고맙네, 어려운 의뢰를 확실히 처리해 주어서.”

“저희 용봉표국은 표행에 있어 한 치의 실수도 용납하지 않습니다.”

“그러니 섬서 제일이라 불리는 것이겠지. 본문도 표국을 운영 중이지만, 역시 용봉표국에 비할 바는 아니야. 허허허.”

주화란은 가슴이 두근거렸다.

황보엄의 칭찬에 기뻐서?

아니었다. 그것과는 무관한, 가슴을 옥죄는 어떤 감정 때문이었다. 그리고 그녀는 그 감정의 이름을 알고 있었다.

불안감.

‘뭔가 잘못됐어.’

그건 예지에 가까운 직감이었다. 그러나 주화란이 불안감의 정체를 더듬어 보기도 전에, 황보엄의 입술이 열렸다.

“자, 이제 마지막 절차만 남았군.”

의뢰한 물품을 확인하고, 인수인계를 증명하기 위해 각자의 수결(手決)을 남긴다.

일다경도 걸리지 않는 간단한 절차 후, 큰 희생을 치른 넉 달간의 표행은 그렇게 마무리될 것이다.

분명 그럴 터였다.

‘……아니, 정말 그럴까?’

지금껏 느껴 본 적 없는 한기가 등줄기를 훑고 올라온다.

얼어붙은 주화란의 귓가로 황보엄의 목소리가 파고들었다.

“뭐 하는 겐가? 어서 물건을 확인시켜 주지 않고.”

주화란은 천천히 고개를 들었다.

인자하고 부드러운 목소리. 그러나 노인의 새카만 눈동자는 묘한 빛으로 번들거리고 있었다.

간신히 쥐어짜 낸 음성이 그녀의 붉은 입술 사이로 흘러나왔다.

“……황보 대협.”

“목곽을 열게. 그 손으로 직접.”

주화란은 깨달았다. 불안감의 정체를, 자신에게는 이제 물러설 곳이 없음을.

결국 그녀에게 남은 선택지는 하나뿐이었다.

스스슥.

가늘게 떨리는 손가락이 매듭을 풀기 시작했다. 주화란이 지난 넉 달 동안 가슴에 품고 있던 목곽이 마치 처음 보는 물건처럼 낯설게 느껴졌다.

‘아니, 아니야. 틀림없어. 절대 그럴 리가…….’

그리고 다음 순간.

달칵.

마침내 목곽이 열리고 내부에 담겨 있던 것이 모습을 드러냈다. 청아한 향기, 곧게 뻗은 뿌리와 서리가 낀 새하얀 몸통.

그것은 틀림없는 설삼(雪三)이었다. 그러나 그 광경을 본 모두가 호흡을 멈추고 눈을 부릅떴다.

그 숨 막히는 정적 속에서 황보엄의 부드러운 목소리가 울렸다.

“재미있군.”

황보엄이 주름진 손가락을 까딱이자 막강한 공력이 흘러나온다.

허공섭물에 의해 두둥실 떠오른 설삼을 바라보며 그가 말을 이었다.

“백년설삼(百年雪蔘)이라…… 지금 노부가 기력이 쇠하여 헛것을 보고 있는 것인가?”

누구를 향한 물음인지는 분명하다.

모두의 시선이 한쪽을 향해 쏠렸다. 경악한 얼굴의 총표두 허준, 없는 사람처럼 삐딱한 자세로 서 있던 송일섬도 마찬가지였다.

수십 쌍의 시선 끝에는 창백한 안색으로 눈을 감고 있는 주화란이 있었다.

‘끝났어.’

목곽 안에 들어 있던 백년설삼을 본 순간, 그녀는 차마 그 광경을 마주하지 못하고 눈을 감아 버렸다.

있을 수도 없고 있어서도 안 되는 일이 벌어졌다.

‘직접 보고, 갖고 있기까지 했는데.’

도대체 어디서부터 어긋난 것일까.

지난 시간이 주마등처럼 캄캄한 눈앞을 스쳐 지나갔다.

그녀는 이번 표행에 용봉표국의 사활을 걸었다.

종남파가 이번 의뢰에 내건 액수는 실로 막대한 거금. 그러나 실패 시 그 열 배에 달하는 위약금을 내야 한다.

그리고 지금, 이 양날의 검은 그녀와 용봉표국의 심장에 틀어박혔다.

“어찌 된 일인지는 묻지 않겠네. 어떤 기상천외한 사정으로 천년설삼이 백년설삼으로 둔갑했는지는 궁금하지 않으니 말이야. 허나…….”

황보엄은 짐짓 안타깝다는 눈빛으로 주화란을 포함한 용봉표국의 사람들을 쓸어 보았다.

“이번 일에 대한 배상은 받아야겠지.”

“……!”

“본문은 이미 천년설삼의 값으로 성수장가에 은자 십만 냥을 지불했네. 그리고 용봉표국이 표행에 성공했을 시, 운송품의 일 할에 해당하는 은자 만 냥을 표비로 지급하기로 했지.”

Ju Hwaran gave a crisp, formal clasped-hands salute.

The Taeeul Merciless Sword, Hwangbo Eom, truly lived up to his reputation. Merely meeting his gaze made her chest tighten and left her struggling to breathe.

*The First Sword of Zhongnan…*

Shandong Seongsu Jang Family.

Anxiety.

*Something is wrong.*

“…Great Hero Hwangbo.”

In the end, only one choice remained.

*Rustle.*

*No. No, that can’t be. I’m certain. There’s no way…*

It was unmistakably snow ginseng. Yet everyone who saw it held their breath, their eyes widening.

Hwangbo Eom’s gentle voice rang through the suffocating silence.

“How amusing.”

He crooked one wrinkled finger, releasing a powerful stream of internal energy.

The snow ginseng floated into the air through Seizing an Object Through Empty Space as he continued.

“A Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng… Is this old man seeing things because his strength has waned?”

At the end of those dozens of gazes stood Ju Hwaran, her face pale and her eyes closed.

The moment she saw the Hundred-Year-Old Snow Ginseng inside the casket, she had shut her eyes, unable to face the sight.

Something that could not and should not have happened had happened.

*I saw it myself. I even kept it in my possession.*

Where had everything gone wrong?

The past few months flashed through the darkness before her eyes like scenes from a dream.

She had staked the Yongbong Escort Bureau’s very survival on this mission.

The Zhongnan Sect had offered an enormous sum for completing it. But if they failed, the Bureau would have to pay ten times that amount as a penalty.

The value of the lost Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng, plus the tenfold penalty the Yongbong Escort Bureau owed for failing to fulfill the contract.

Blood ran from Ju Hwaran’s lips as the realization struck her, and Chief Escort Heo Jun’s face went black.

“G-Great Hero Hwangbo, that is…!”

“Two hundred thousand silver nyang. I will permit no compromise.”

“A-Ah…”

The escorts who had accompanied Ju Hwaran groaned in despair.

Every one of them except Song Ilseom.

“Very good. I feel as though I’ve gone back thirty years.”

“……!”

“What’s wrong? Drink before it gets cold.”

She had been completely outmaneuvered. Even after taking every precaution, she had still fallen into the trap.

*Can I rise again like before?*

*We can pay the penalty.*

It was possible.

They would have to sell every field and parcel of land owned by the Yongbong Escort Bureau for a pittance, then send away the hundreds of caravan porters, escorts, and Escort Captains whose wages they could no longer afford.

And once that entire process was over, nothing would remain of the Yongbong Escort Bureau but an empty shell.

*Is it really over? Just like this?*

Hwangbo Eom watched Ju Hwaran with amusement.

He had long heard that the Young Bureau Head of the Yongbong Escort Bureau was quite capable.

*Heh. How pitiful.*

Just as Hwangbo Eom chuckled inwardly—

*This is…*

The qi was so powerful that even Hwangbo Eom, a Supreme Peak master, could not easily ignore it.

A vast reserve of internal energy comparable to that of an Elder from the Nine Sects and One Gang steadily approached, then stopped directly outside the teahouse.

*Could it be Huashan?*

Hwangbo Eom’s prediction was proven spectacularly wrong the next moment.

*Creaaak.*

“Oh, I was just in the mood for some tea, and look at that! A teahouse, right when I needed one.”

A broad-shouldered young man opened the door and strode in at the head of the group.

Hwangbo Eom’s eyes darkened as he looked at Jin Taekyung.

* * *

Even at a glance, it was an unusual sight.

Dozens of swordsmen stood throughout the room, and the air hung heavy.

*Ju Hwaran—or rather, the Yongbong Escort Bureau?*

The question had barely crossed my mind when I spotted them.

On top of a table surrounded by people, slender fingers trembled faintly.

I had only met her once, but I could tell who she was just from her fingers. Funny how that worked.

*Were her hands pretty?*

As I scratched the back of my head, everyone’s gaze flew toward me.

A middle-aged man who appeared to be the owner of the teahouse hurried over, bowing repeatedly.

“Sir, I’m sorry, but we’re completely full right now…”

“There’s a seat over there.”

“That seat isn’t in use.”

“Then I’ll drink standing up.”

At that moment, a martial artist who appeared to be a Disciple of the Zhongnan Sect approached with measured steps.

“Are you a martial artist?”

“No, I’m fat.”

The martial artist looked me up and down as if he were staring at a complete lunatic.

“I don’t know who you are or where you come from, but an important person is here right now. You would do well to leave.”

“I’m an important son in my own family too, so why should I? There’s plenty of room anyway.”

“……You’re being troublesome. I am a Disciple of the Great Zhongnan Sect. You should understand by now, so leave.”

“Why do you keep ordering me around? I just want to sit down and have some tea.”

Cheongpung, who had been fidgeting behind me, shouted excitedly.

“Benefactor! Candied sweets too!”

“Candied sweets? Hey, Mujin. Does this teahouse sell those too?”

“Are you seriously saying that right now?”

*What the hell is wrong with these guys?*

The Zhongnan Sect disciple had been looking at us as if to say exactly that, but his face stiffened when he spotted someone.

“H-Huashan’s Lone Crane, Baek Museong!”

Maybe it was because this was Huashan’s home ground, but quite a few people here recognized Baek Museong.

In any case, the Zhongnan Disciple’s involuntary shout had an immediate effect. Unlike when we first entered, everyone was looking at us now.

Two gazes stood out from the rest.

I waved at one of them.

“Oh, we meet again.”

“…Young Hero Jin?”

Ju Hwaran stared at me with her pale face and wide, round eyes.

Across from her sat an old man with a long white beard.

I gave Ju Hwaran a small smile, then gazed at the old man.

“Is there some problem between you and Young Lady Ju?”

The old man—the Taeeul Merciless Sword, Hwangbo Eom—stroked his beard and laughed.

“An interesting fellow has appeared.”

“H-Huashan’s Lone Crane, Baek Museong!”

Maybe it was because this was Huashan’s home ground, but quite a few people here recognized Baek Museong.

In any case, the Zhongnan Disciple’s involuntary shout had an immediate effect. Unlike when we first entered, everyone was looking at us now.

Ju Hwaran stared at me with her pale face and wide, round eyes.

The old man—the Taeeul Merciless Sword, Hwangbo Eom—stroked his beard and laughed.

“An interesting fellow has appeared.”

“I am Ju Hwaran, Young Bureau Head of the Yongbong Escort Bureau. I pay my respects to Great Hero Hwangbo, the Taeeul Merciless Sword.”

Ju Hwaran gave a crisp, formal clasped-hands salute.

*The First Sword of Zhongnan…*

The Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families—the fifteen pillars supporting the Murim of today.

The man before her was the greatest master of the Zhongnan Sect, one of those fifteen powers. The immense weight of his name pressed down on her.

*But it’s all right.*

She had completed an escort mission everyone had agreed was impossible.

That was why she could stand tall even if the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord himself had come instead of the Taeeul Merciless Sword.

“Well? Did you bring the item I requested?”

“Of course.”

Shandong Seongsu Jang Family.

Hwangbo Eom checked the writing and nodded.

“No mistake. It bears the seal of the Seongsu Jang Family.”

People said that if Sichuan had the Tang Family, then Shandong had the Seongsu Jang Family.

That was how renowned the Seongsu Jang Family was for its medical arts. Unlike the Sichuan Tang Clan, a Murim great family, it was a prestigious medical family with its roots in medicine.

The Zhongnan Sect had purchased the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng through that very family and entrusted its transportation to the Yongbong Escort Bureau.

“The Pill Physician, the current Family Head of the Seongsu Jang Family, personally placed the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng inside and signed the casket.”

“Oh? The Pill Physician himself?”

“Yes. Several witnesses, myself included, watched the entire process.”

“You’re remarkably thorough for someone your age.”

Hwangbo Eom stroked his white beard with wrinkled fingers.

“This old man has heard that the Junzi Sword’s[^1] daughter is a gifted young woman. Thank you for handling such a difficult assignment so reliably.”

“Our Yongbong Escort Bureau does not tolerate even the slightest mistake on an escort mission.”

“That must be why you’re called the best in Shaanxi. Our sect operates an Escort Bureau as well, but it cannot compare with yours. Ha ha ha.”

Ju Hwaran’s heart pounded.

Was it because Hwangbo Eom had praised her?

No. It had nothing to do with his praise. Something else was constricting her chest, and she knew the name of that feeling.

Anxiety.

*Something is wrong.*

It was an intuition bordering on foresight. But before Ju Hwaran could even begin to trace its source, Hwangbo Eom spoke.

“Well, only the final procedure remains.”

They would inspect the requested item, then each leave their signature to certify that the handover was complete.

After a simple procedure that would take less than the time needed to drink a cup of tea, the four-month escort mission that had cost them so dearly would finally come to an end.

That was how it was supposed to happen.

A chill unlike anything she had ever felt crept up her spine.

Hwangbo Eom’s voice pierced her frozen ears.

“What are you waiting for? Show me the item.”

Ju Hwaran slowly raised her head.

His voice was kind and gentle, yet the old man’s pitch-black eyes gleamed with a strange light.

She barely managed to force the words past her red lips.

“…Great Hero Hwangbo.”

“Open the casket. With your own hands.”

Ju Hwaran realized it then—the source of her anxiety, and that she had nowhere left to retreat.

In the end, only one choice remained.

*Rustle.*

Her slender, trembling fingers began to untie the knot. The wooden casket she had kept close to her heart for the past four months suddenly felt alien, as though she were seeing it for the first time.

*No. No, that can’t be. I’m certain. There’s no way…*

And then—

*Click.*

It was unmistakably snow ginseng. Yet everyone who saw it held their breath, their eyes widening.

Hwangbo Eom’s gentle voice rang through the suffocating silence.

“How amusing.”

He crooked one wrinkled finger, releasing a powerful stream of internal energy.

The snow ginseng floated into the air through Seizing an Object Through Empty Space as he continued.

It was obvious who the question was meant for.

She had staked the Yongbong Escort Bureau’s very survival on this mission.

The Zhongnan Sect had offered an enormous sum for completing it. But if they failed, the Bureau would have to pay ten times that amount as a penalty.

“……!”

He had long heard that the Young Bureau Head of the Yongbong Escort Bureau was quite capable.

Hwangbo Eom’s eyes darkened as he looked at Jin Taekyung.
